web_evidence.title: Book excerpt: "James" by Percival Everett
web_evidence.note: A sustained excerpt published with Doubleday’s permission opens in Jim’s first-person voice and distinguishes his narration from surrounding dialogue.

web_evidence.title: A Story of His Own
web_evidence.note: This detailed review explicitly identifies James as the first-person narrator and follows that narrating position through opening and later episodes across the novel.

web_evidence.title: James Reading Group Guide
web_evidence.note: Penguin Random House’s guide repeatedly calls the voice “Jim’s narration” and frames Jim as the narrator of his own story across the novel.

search_log: Searched “Percival Everett James novel excerpt first chapter publisher,” “James Percival Everett first person narrator point of view review,” and narrator/interview variants.
Searched Penguin Random House domains for an authorized excerpt and reading guide; opened the official reading guide and publisher product page.
Opened the CBS excerpt and verified that it is a sustained opening passage reproduced by permission of Doubleday.
Opened the New York Review of Books review and verified its explicit identification of James as the first-person narrator across its discussion of the novel.

Searched exact quotations to distinguish base narration from local speech or Jim’s embedded notebook writing; search results clarified the notebook context of “With my pencil, I wrote myself into being.”
A Penguin Random House Germany excerpt PDF and a Taylor & Francis scholarly article appeared in search results but could not be opened successfully, so neither was used as evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator is Jim/James, a participant who tells his own story in the first person. Numerous Goodreads passages from varied interior situations independently expose sustained “I” and “we” narration, while dialogue-only aphorisms and Jim’s locally embedded notebook declaration were not allowed to vote mechanically. The authorized opening excerpt confirms the same voice, and the whole-book NYRB analysis plus the publisher’s guide identify Jim as narrator without indicating any sustained change of person. The isolated “I am James” declaration is treated as speech, not separate narration. No credible evidence of alternating or second-/third-person base sections was found.
